note: THE one deadline policy. Readers (load_policy.READERS, checked by selftest_bridge_deadlines.py): launch_ready.py (launch_and_wait.sh), belt_watchdog.py, live_session.py, FlowWorks playtest_runner.py and rimbridge_client.py; never restate these numbers in code or docs. Proposed conservative defaults (GPT review 2026-10-10 s4.4), NOT measured healthy-load limits. Observed full-list loads: ~15 min (599 mods, 2026-09-07), 18.5-21 min (five loads, 2026-10-03). kill_on_deadline is false and must stay false: a deadline ends the ATTEMPT, it never declares the game hung; a stall verdict needs evidence (log frozen, CPU idle, Not Responding), never the clock alone. call_deadline is absolute: a bridge call's limit is one monotonic instant fixed when the request is sent; events or bytes arriving never extend it (GPT N04). Every deadline-exceeded message says whether the game process is ALIVE, DEAD or UNKNOWN (load_policy.deadline_exceeded). late_arrival_watch_s (LAUNCHREADY_FIX_CRITERION_STEAM_REVIVES, a chosen default, not measured): after LAUNCH_NO_PROCESS the launcher keeps watching that long and kills by PID any game our launch started late, so the verdict stays true; a steam:// launch revives a closed Steam, observed starting the game in 9 s (2026-10-31).
